query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: problem_domain
per_column.rationale: Categorises incidents into problem areas derived cleanly from short_description; gives a genuine grouping axis to compare resolution times across domains. Evidence rows all map soundly (VPN->vpn_connectivity, database->database_connectivity).

per_column.name: incident_severity_urgency
per_column.rationale: Severity/urgency is a plausible strong predictor of resolution time, so it is useful. However groundedness is weaker: mapping 'Email system not working properly' to service_degraded vs 'Cannot connect to database' to user_blocked involves inference beyond the terse text, and priority is already an original column so some values may not be well warranted.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Blast radius (system-wide vs user-level) is a reasonable driver of resolution time and a useful axis. Department-specific readings ('sales department', 'Marketing Department') are grounded, but many system_wide/user_level assignments (e.g. 'VPN connection issue' -> user_level) are inferences the text does not clearly support.

per_column.name: resolution_ownership_mismatch
per_column.rationale: A mismatch between assignee and closer could plausibly signal harder incidents, so mildly useful. It is nearly constant (461 false), reducing analytical leverage, and its derivation from assigned_to/closed_by is only partially verifiable; the near-degenerate distribution limits value.

per_column.name: technical_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with problem_domain (network/application/database mirror the same categories) so it adds little new leverage. Values are a reasonable reading of short_description, but 'generic_outage' and the complexity framing over-assert specificity not present in the terse text.

per_column.name: responder_expertise_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Whether the responder matched the domain (or needed escalation) is a strong candidate signal for longer resolution, hence useful. But groundedness is weak: the table lacks responder skill/domain metadata, so 'domain_expert_assigned' vs 'escalation_required' is largely inferred and cannot be soundly derived from available fields.

per_column.name: incident_closure_status
per_column.rationale: Directly readable from state/closed_at, so well grounded, but trivially redundant with existing original columns (state, closed_at) and does not itself indicate resolution duration, giving little new analytical leverage for this query.

judge.rationale: Several columns give genuine grouping axes (problem_domain, severity, scope, responder mismatch) directly relevant to predicting slower resolution. Weaknesses: technical_complexity_signal duplicates problem_domain, incident_closure_status restates original fields, and resolution_ownership_mismatch is near-constant. Groundedness is generally acceptable for extraction-style columns but drops where the operator asserts responder expertise or severity/scope specifics the terse source text does not clearly support.
